title: The Reform — a political party built as a palace
learning_goal: Know that this club was built to fight the one down the road, and that it did the work a party headquarters does now.

narration.script: Budgeted at thirty-seven and a half thousand pounds. It finished at eighty-two. Six floors, three of them below the street — kitchens and the engine that heats the whole house underneath everything. In the eighteen-thirties a club did the work a party headquarters does now: registering voters, whipping, picking candidates. This one opened with a thousand members, nearly two hundred and fifty of them MPs, to counter the Tory club down the road. A celebrity chef in 1837. Alexis Soyer helped design these kitchens, then published them as a book. People came to tour a basement. A members' library of eighty-five thousand volumes, all of it donated — which is why a member needed no study at home.
